package_info.package_versions: 7.x, 8.8.x, 8.9.x, 9.0.x (all maintained versions at time of disclosure)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Drupal core contain a critical DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (DOM XSS) vulnerability (CVE-2020-13663) and a Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2020-13663), which allow attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the site, potentially leading to full site compromise, data theft, and privilege escalation.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with web forms or DOM elements)
execution_context.file_location: Drupal core Form API (PHP/JS code handling form input and DOM manipulation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code takes unsanitized user input from the DOM (e.g., URL hash or form field), injects it directly into the page's HTML via innerHTML, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution in the context of the site.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly inserting unsanitized user input into the DOM is a classic XSS vector, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or encode user input before rendering it in the DOM; the actual behavior fails to do so, enabling XSS.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve rendering user-generated content after proper sanitization/escaping.
key_indicators: Unsanitized user input rendered in DOM
Use of innerHTML or similar DOM APIs with attacker-controlled data
No input validation or output encoding

execution_context.file_location: Drupal core Form API (PHP code handling form input from HTTP requests)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes form input from HTTP POST requests without validating CSRF tokens, allowing attackers to forge requests on behalf of authenticated users.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Processing sensitive form actions without CSRF protection allows attackers to perform actions as the victim user.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would require a valid CSRF token for state-changing requests; the actual behavior omits this check.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would always include CSRF token validation for sensitive actions.
key_indicators: Absence of CSRF token validation in form processing
Sensitive actions triggered by POST requests without anti-CSRF measures

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious link or form input containing JavaScript payload or forged request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim user (including admin) interacts with the malicious input.

attack_chain.action: Malicious input is processed by Drupal core without proper sanitization or CSRF validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary JavaScript executes in victim's browser or sensitive actions are performed as the victim.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to victim's session, escalates privileges, or exfiltrates sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full site compromise, data theft, or privilege escalation.

behavioral_signatures: Unsanitized user input rendered in the DOM (e.g., innerHTML with attacker-controlled data)
Form submissions processed without CSRF token validation
Unexpected JavaScript execution in admin or user context
file_indicators: Custom or core Drupal modules that use innerHTML or similar DOM APIs with user input
Form processing code lacking CSRF token checks
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests to Drupal endpoints without CSRF tokens
Requests containing suspicious payloads in form fields or URL fragments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Review Drupal core and custom module code for instances where user input is inserted into the DOM without sanitization (e.g., innerHTML, document.write). Audit form processing logic to ensure CSRF tokens are required and validated for all state-changing actions. Monitor web traffic for suspicious form submissions or URL fragments containing script tags or suspicious payloads. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to block common XSS and CSRF attack patterns.
